messages:
maria: FYI customer ACME (ticket #23456) reporting SSE stream is cutting out mid-response when the user switches from 5G -> WiFi. They get ~40% of the JSON then the connection closes. They see a client reconnect that replays the request and the billing meter shows two partial charges. Repro steps below.

sam: ugh. any error codes in the logs from our side? do we see socket close reason or 4xx? :thinking_face:

maria: logs show repeated `socket: read tcp ...: i/o timeout` and then the client immediately opens a new SSE connection. our access logs show the first stream ended with 200 but truncated body, then a new POST started ~1s later. no 5xx from us. snippet:

olivia: can you paste the raw logs? also which SDK and client OS? mobile or web?

maria: customer on iOS 16.5 (third-party app), using our JS streaming SDK (v0.8.2). they included an excerpt:

```
[2026-03-15T14:02:11.123Z] conn_id=abc123 stream: event chunk size=2048
[2026-03-15T14:02:12.457Z] conn_id=abc123 socket: read tcp 10.0.0.3:54321->34.56.78.90:443: i/o timeout
[2026-03-15T14:02:12.458Z] conn_id=abc123 stream: client closed, partial bytes 11234
[2026-03-15T14:02:13.700Z] conn_id=def456 auth: token refresh started
[2026-03-15T14:02:14.001Z] conn_id=def456 stream: new stream started
```

kyle: looks like a client-side TCP timeout on network handoff. i/o timeout suggests the socket stalled during in-flight data. do they set keepalive or a heartbeat? our default SSE connection timeout is long; we shouldn't cut the stream proactively.

jessica: customer also mentioned token rotation. they refresh the bearer token immediately after detecting disconnect, and the SDK auto-retries the same request. that explains duplicate billing. we should check idempotency or recommend application-level dedupe for partial responses.

maria: repro steps they gave (we asked them to try a repro):
1) start a streaming completion that returns ~20k tokens (we used a long doc summarization)
2) while streaming, toggle mobile data off to force a handoff to WiFi (or turn on hotspot on another device)
3) watch for partial json chunk + immediate reconnect from SDK

They included a curl-based repro we asked them to try:

```
# streaming via curl (simulate mobile client)
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Client-Heartbeat: 15" \
  -d '{"prompt":"<very long prompt>", "max_tokens":20000}' \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-xl"
```

kyle: that `X-Client-Heartbeat` header is user-level. our platform supports server-side keepalive but only for connection-level; if the client toggles network the TCP stack often kills the socket and the app-level reconnect logic fires. the interesting bit is the partial JSON — are we flushing SSE frames mid-chunk? could the client be writing partial chunk to disk then failing to parse?

eng-runtime-bot: escalate: attach logs + pcap if customer can capture. potential follow-ups: investigate whether our SSE framing is robust to abrupt TCP close during a chunk boundary and whether the SDK retries result in duplicate server-side processing.

olivia: for triage i want to reproduce locally. can someone try with the SDK in a simulator and flip airplane mode? if we can get a deterministic repro we can test different keepalive intervals.

sam: quick mitigation suggestions to give customer:
- set the SDK to not auto-retry streaming requests on disconnect (or debounce retries by 5s)
- enable client heartbeats (send a comment/event every 10s)
- add a client-side dedupe: attach a client-generated idempotency key to the request metadata so server can return cached partial if retried

jessica: note on billing: currently we meter tokens written to the response stream. partial responses count. product flagged this as acceptable billing behavior but wants clearer messaging and possible credits when a clear network handoff causes duplicate partial charges. @finance FYI.

maria: ask to eng-runtime: can you check whether we ever mark a streaming request as "complete" before the final SSE delimiter is flushed? also, any hooks where an aborted stream could leave transient work done that gets re-run on retry?

eng-runtime-bot: acked. action items for eng-runtime:
- reproduce with SDK + airplane-mode flip
- run server under tcpdump and watch for FIN/RST/timeout behavior at chunk boundaries
- check idempotency path: can a retried streaming call re-run the workload or is it a resumed stream? (we currently do not support resume mid-stream)

kyle: assigning to @eng-runtime on pager. tagging priority P2 for now unless customer revenue impact is severe. maria, can you ask for a short pcap and the exact SDK settings? also ask for approximate data usage pattern and whether they have proxy/MITM.

maria: will get pcap and SDK config. customer asked if we can provide a server-side workaround in the meantime — they want a short-term suggestion to avoid double charges.

sam: short-term: recommend disabling immediate retry and add client-side dedupe keys. we can also offer to issue a bill credit manually if they provide evidence of network handoff causing duplicate charge. please open a billing support ticket for review.

maria: thanks all — collecting artifacts from customer now. will update thread when I have pcap + SDK config. :thumbsup:
